we present an architecture that can learn new tasks in an online fashion while not suffering from catastrophic forgetting, that we show this architecture is capable of solving a variety of reinforcement learning tasks, and that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods for continual learning in reinforcement learning.

we have devised a novel method, Self- Activating Neural Ensembles, which does not suffer from catastrophic forgetting in a task agnostic manner, and which can learn new skills as needed.

SANE is a new approach to the problem of continual reinforcement learning that is able to avoid catastrophic forgetting in a task agnostic manner.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SANE is an effective method for learning a set of skills in a continuous fashion, without any assumptions on the task structure.
SANE is a novel method for continual reinforcement learning that is capable of learning new tasks without forgetting existing knowledge.
we have devised a novel approach to continual learning which is task-agnostic and does not require well-defined task boundaries to function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
task-agnostic lifelong learning is possible without task boundaries.
task-agnostic continual learning is feasible, and can be achieved without making strong task assumptions.

task agnosticism and continual learning can be achieved with a single method that does not require the use of external memory, task-specific architectures or hand-crafted heuristics to avoid catastrophic forgetting.
